anatomy.intro: One opposite leaf pair forms the stone-like body around a central cleft.

parts.function: A fleshy leaf holds water that can support the next pair.
parts.label: Thick leaf

parts.function: Fine spotting contributes to the stone-like appearance.
parts.label: Speckled surface

parts.function: The opening separates the opposing leaves and allows new growth to emerge.
parts.label: Central cleft

parts.function: The opposite leaves are joined at their lower base.
parts.label: Joined base

flowers.text: Flowers emerge between the leaves and resemble large daisies. The nursery listing conflicts on 'Royal Flush' color, describing golden flowers in prose and pink in its product field; this collection's bloom color remains unrecorded.

growth.note: Follow the visible stage rather than a month-based schedule; wrinkling outer leaves during renewal does not alone call for watering.

stages.text: A compact pair forms the main visible plant.

stages.text: The cleft opens around an emerging inner pair.
stages.title: Reveal new leaves

stages.text: Older leaves lose stored water and eventually dry as the new pair develops.
stages.title: Use the outer pair

habitat.text: Wild Pleiospilos nelii occurs among sparse Karoo vegetation near the Western and Eastern Cape boundary in South Africa. Its rounded, speckled leaves resemble surrounding stones. 'Royal Flush' is a cultivated pink-purple form; the species habitat explains its structure but does not establish the origin or exact seasonal behavior of this nursery plant.

Pleiospilos nelii Royal Flush: one single stemless split-rock plant, exactly TWO thick purple-mauve egg-shaped leaves forming ONE opposite leaf pair, joined at their low base, deep central cleft and fine dark speckles over the surfaces. Three-quarter close view, a few loose ground pebbles, leave lower joined base clearly visible. No inner new leaves at all, no flowers. Four numbered leaders: 1 points to the broad thick left leaf, 2 points to speckles on upper right leaf, 3 points into the central fissure between the pair, 4 points to the low joined base where the two leaves meet just above the soil. lookalikes.name: Green split rock
lookalikes.text: The same probable species can have grey-green leaves rather than the seller-labeled purple 'Royal Flush' coloring. Color supports comparison but does not independently authenticate a cultivar.

mature.text: The nursery lists roughly 3–5 inches high and 3–4 inches across. This is a compact leaf succulent, not a stem-forming shrub; several persistent stacked pairs are not the intended mature silhouette.

nameStory.text: Pleiospilos refers to its many spots. The species' woody seed capsules open when wet, letting raindrops release some seeds before the capsules close again as they dry.
